chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is not befitting for the woman that she uncovers herself in front of the Jewish woman and the Christian woman, for they describe that to their husbands.

key_terms.بَيْنَ يَدَيِ: in front of / in the presence of

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a Muslim woman uncovering herself in front of Jewish and Christian women?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the principle of 'satr' (covering) within the specific social context of early Islamic Medina, where interactions with Ahl al-Kitab were common. It underscores the practical wisdom of maintaining modesty not just for piety, but to prevent inadvertent exposure through the descriptive habits of non-Muslim women, reflecting the Shia emphasis on contextual legal rulings (fiqh).

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It is not befitting for the woman that she uncovers herself in front of the Jewish women and the Christian women, for they can describe that to their husbands’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is not proper for a woman to remove her veil before a Jewish woman or a Christian woman because they can describe it to their husband.’”
